newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Beirut names bond issue managers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Beirut names bond issue managers.

text.p: Paribas and Beirut-based Middle East Capital Group (MECG) have been appointed joint lead managers for a three-year $50 million Euro-offering by Bank of Beirut, MECG said in a statement on Friday.

The issue is expected to be launched in the first half of May, the statement said. It will be offered to international and regional investors and the notes will be listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.
Bank of Beirut is the fourth Lebanese bank to announce or issue debt on the international market this year.

Banque Mediterranee issued a $50 million five-year Eurobond in March, Banque Libano-Francaise issued a $125 million EuroCD on Thursday and Byblos Bank has said it will issue the first $100 million tranche of a $300 million Euronote programme in the second quarter.
Thursday's Libano-Francaise issue brought to $595 million the total of international debt that Lebanese commercial banks have raised since last June.

Bank of Beirut is a small but growing bank which ranked 16th in total assets and 13th in net profit in 1996 among Lebanon's 82 banks. Its shares have jumped 64 percent since listing on the Beirut Stock Exchange on April 11.
